e.etymology: From Sanskrit dhriti, firmness, constancy or resolve, a virtue named in the Bhagavad Gita and the name of a Hindu goddess.
A modern Hebrew name, the feminine of ilan, tree. In English it is sometimes also treated as a spelling of Alana.
namesakes: Ilana Glazer (comedian and co-creator of Broad City)

e.etymology: From Arabic jalil, great, exalted or majestic. Al-Jalil is one of the names of God in Islam.
namesakes: Jaleel White (actor who played Steve Urkel on Family Matters)

assoc.t: Jaleel White, who played Steve Urkel

e.etymology: A recent name of unclear source, close in sound to Zara, Amara and Azaria. Azara is also a Spanish surname.
A recent name with no single settled source. It is read either as a pet form of Mavis and Maeve or as French ma vie, my life, run together.
A pet form of Elizabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath. Lizzie was often given as a full name in the United States in the late 1800s.
namesakes: Lizzie Borden (acquitted of the 1892 Fall River axe murders)
Lizzie McGuire (Disney Channel character played by Hilary Duff)

assoc.t: Tin Lizzie, nickname of the Ford Model T

e.etymology: A phonetic American spelling of Dante, the Italian short form of Durante, from Latin durans, enduring. Dante is given in honor of the poet Dante Alighieri.

e.meaning: the mahogany tree and its reddish-brown wood
e.etymology: From the tropical hardwood and its rich reddish-brown color; the source of the word is unknown. The 1975 Diana Ross film Mahogany helped bring it into use as a name.

assoc.t: mahogany, the reddish-brown hardwood and color
Mahogany, 1975 Diana Ross film and its theme song

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that joins the Jaz- of Jasmine and Jazlyn to the -elle ending of Giselle and Gabrielle.

In Chinese, most often the character mei meaning beautiful, or another mei meaning plum blossom. In Japanese, Mei is a separate name written with various characters, such as those for bud and for bright.
namesakes: Mei Lee (heroine of Pixar's Turning Red)
Mei Kusakabe (little sister in My Neighbor Totoro)

assoc.t: Mei Lee, the girl who becomes a red panda in Turning Red

e.etymology: A spelling of Maisie, the Scottish pet form of Mairead (Margaret), from Greek margarites, pearl.
A Dutch short name known from Washington Irving's Rip Van Winkle, and a nickname for Ripley. Its current use follows Rip Wheeler, the ranch foreman of the TV series Yellowstone.
namesakes: Rip Van Winkle (Washington Irving's man who slept twenty years)
Rip Torn (actor in Men in Black)

assoc.t: RIP, short for rest in peace
Rip Wheeler of the series Yellowstone
rip, the everyday word for a tear

e.note: Reads as RIP (rest in peace) and as the verb rip, so expect jokes.

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that puts the Jay sound in front of -lani, on the model of Kailani and Leilani, whose Hawaiian lani means sky or heaven.
A pet form of Roberta or Barbara, written with a feminine -i. Roberta is the feminine of Robert, from Germanic hrod, fame, and berht, bright.
namesakes: Bobbi Brown (makeup artist who founded the cosmetics line)
Bobbi Kristina Brown (daughter of Whitney Houston)

e.etymology: The Spanish form of Dominic, from Late Latin Dominicus, of the Lord. Domingo is also the Spanish word for Sunday, and the name was traditionally given to boys born on that day.
namesakes: Colman Domingo (actor in Rustin and Sing Sing)

assoc.t: Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic
Domingo, recurring Saturday Night Live character

e.etymology: From Latin Octavius, the name of a Roman family, from octavus, eighth. The emperor Augustus was born Gaius Octavius.

assoc.t: Dr. Otto Octavius, Spider-Man's Doctor Octopus

e.etymology: A spelling of Aisha, from Arabic aisha, alive or living. Aisha bint Abi Bakr was a wife of the Prophet Muhammad and a major source of early Islamic teaching.
A modern coinage that joins May to -lani, the Hawaiian word for sky or heaven, on the model of Leilani and Kailani. It is also written Mailani.
A modern elaboration of Nova, Latin for new and the word for a star that suddenly brightens. Its model is Novalee Nation, heroine of the novel and film Where the Heart Is.
A spelling of Collins, an English surname meaning son of Colin, a medieval pet form of Nicholas. Collins took off for girls after the 2009 film The Blind Side, which featured Collins Tuohy.
An English surname from Brenton in Devon, Old English for the settlement of a man named Bryni.
Usually taken as a form of Xenia, from Greek xenia, hospitality, or as a short form of Zenobia. It sounds the same as Xena.
The German short form of Johannes, from Latin Iohannes and Greek Ioannes, from Hebrew Yochanan, Yahweh is gracious. It is the German equivalent of John.
namesakes: Johann Strauss II (composer known as the Waltz King)
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (German poet, author of Faust)

e.etymology: The Hebrew form of Deborah, from devorah, bee. In the Book of Judges, Deborah is a prophet and judge who leads Israel to victory.
A modern American coinage in the family of Amari, Jamari and Kamari. It is also close to Samara and to Samaria, the Biblical region.
A Japanese name most often written with the character for dragon, borrowed from Middle Chinese. Other characters with the same reading are also used. Ryu is also a Korean surname.
namesakes: Ryu (karate fighter and lead character of Street Fighter)

assoc.t: Ryu, the lead fighter of the Street Fighter games

e.etymology: A respelling of Kinsley, an English surname from a Yorkshire place name: the clearing of a man named Cyne, a short name from Old English cyne, royal.
A modern Indian name, popular alongside Vihaan, Ishaan and Reyansh. Baby-name sources often link it with the god Shiva, but its Sanskrit derivation is not well documented.
The Arabic form of Solomon, from Hebrew Shelomoh, tied to shalom, peace. Sulayman is a prophet and king in the Quran, and Suleiman the Magnificent ruled the Ottoman Empire at its height.

e.meaning: moon flood, moonlight; also glossed as moon beauty
e.etymology: A Turkish and Azerbaijani name built on ay, moon. It is usually read as ay plus sel, flood or stream, a flood of moonlight; some sources instead gloss it as beautiful moon.
A spelling of Callum, the Scottish Gaelic form of the Latin name Columba, dove. Saint Columba founded the monastery of Iona in the 6th century.
A recent name with no settled source, close in sound to Yael, Azael and Zaid.
